title: Actual compact-support tower reduction and its coefficient-independent bounds
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, and put $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_{E,en}$ for $n\geq1$. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their uniform constructible finite-Tor full subcategories $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and ordinary derived tensor products [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$ with finite units, counits and evaluations is [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Put $\mathbf1_{\bullet,T}=(R_{n,T})_n$ and $\omega_\bullet=G_\bullet\mathbf1_{\bullet,Y}$, so $\omega_n=f^!_{R_n}R_{n,Y}$; pullback means levelwise finite derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $C_\bullet\in\mathcal C_X$ and write $\rho^C_{n,m}:(C_n)_{R_m}\to C_m$ for its canonical reduction maps [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]; no normalization is assumed. Choose a compactification $f=pj$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and compute $F_\bullet=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ using [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Under its finite evaluations, the actual reduction maps of this derived strict tower are
$$\rho^{FC}_{n,m}=Rf_{!,R_m}(\rho^C_{n,m})\circ b_{R_n,R_m}(C_n)\qquad(1\leq m\leq n),$$
where $b$ is precisely the compactification-normalized coefficient comparison [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]: the proper coefficient exchange, followed by the extension-by-zero tensor identification. These identities include identity indices and the quotient composition cocycle. For common input Tor bounds $[a,b]$, the levels of $F_\bullet C_\bullet$ are constructible and have common Tor and cohomological bounds $[a,b+2d]$, so $F_\bullet C_\bullet\in\mathcal C_Y$. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $R_m$ over $R_n$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the finite Evaluation for the supplied base, operations and coordinates: whisker the realization counit, the existing Fcomparison of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], and the two levelComparison isomorphisms. Expanding this word proves the required normalization. The bounded constructible essential-image criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] gives each input level an etale representative; transport its bounded-below origin through the intrinsic derived equivalence. Together these constructions supply FiniteNormalization without choosing new operations or assuming preservation.

Derive characteristic p of the closure field from the recorded finite-field cardinality. QuasiCompact.of_comp gives quasi-compactness of f, and Compactification.quasiCompact_openImmersion gives it for the chosen open factor. Smooth relative dimension survives base change by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]; the proved upstream topologicalKrullDim_le_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension bounds each geometric fibre by d, including empty fibres. For every positive quotient prove ell^(n+1)=0 by ideal membership; since ell differs from p its exponent is invertible on Spec k. Apply the proved finite_bound helper of [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] to the level and its prescribed Tor interval. Its output gives finite-Tor constructibility, Tor interval [a,b+2d], and cohomology vanishing in that interval. Whisker the canonical open-coordinate isomorphism and inverse Evaluation to transport all three conclusions to the actual output level. Apply this to the common input Tor interval from [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] to obtain the output tower predicate, and to an arbitrary supplied interval to obtain the final quantitative clause.

Use finite_coordinates_exists from [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] for the section-preserving direct-image coordinates. Apply [lem-sp-tower-transition-compatibility] to the supplied operations, the FiniteNormalization constructed in step 1, and the input tower. This gives exactly the displayed equation for every m <= n with the canonical comparison of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Unlike the existential full calculus theorem, this transition theorem works for the already supplied base and operations and needs no global preservation hypothesis.

Apply the already proved reduction_identity_aux and reduction_composition_aux from [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus] to the actual output tower. These helpers expand the intrinsic scalar coordinates and use respectively reduction_identity and reduction_comp from [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. They yield the displayed scalar-unit and scalar-associator equations without requiring any reduction to be invertible.
